references.text: Hobab, son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses' father-in-law, is mentioned here. This establishes the connection between Moses and the Kenites through his father-in-law.
Reuel, the priest in Midian, was Moses' father-in-law. Moses married his daughter Zipporah, which links Moses to the Kenites.
Jericho is called 'the city of palms', the same city referred to as 'the city of palms' in this verse from where the Kenites departed.
Arad in the Negev is mentioned here in connection with Israel's battle against the Canaanites, the same geographical area where the Kenites settled.
Saul warned the Kenites before he attacked the Amalekites, because the Kenites had shown kindness to the Israelites when they came up from Egypt.
The Negev region of the Kenites is mentioned as a place David plundered, showing the presence of the Kenites in this area.
The cities of the Kenites are listed among the places David sent spoils of war to, confirming their settlement in the Judah region.
Heber the Kenite had separated from the Kenites, descendants of Hobab, Moses' father-in-law, and settled near Kedesh.
